decisions.reason: As a newly launched resin injection unit that fits the firm's core application and fluid-handling capabilities, it is likely to be retained while management gathers more market feedback rather than reallocating resources immediately.

This second resin injection unit is close to the firm's established technical base and customer needs, so under bounded rationality the firm would usually keep it for another year unless clear underperformance emerges.
An automatic airless spray gun is strongly aligned with the firm's long-standing spray equipment business, making continued support more likely than withdrawal at this early stage.
A manual airless spray gun sits at the heart of the firm's established product-market domain, so aspiration levels are likely easier to meet and the product is unlikely to be dropped quickly.
The air-assisted airless spray gun extends a familiar technology platform for existing industrial customers, so the firm would typically keep it on the market while learning about demand.

The data logger is more experimental than the mechanical core products and may face higher uncertainty, but it supports the firm's innovation direction and is still likely to be kept while its market potential is assessed.
